preconditions.description: n is the number of nodes (2 ≤ n ≤ 200,000) and k is the number of nodes inspected (1 ≤ k ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: len(a) == int(n) and all(1 <= int(x) <= 1000000 for x in a.split())
preconditions.description: a is a list of n integers (1 ≤ ai ≤ 1,000,000) representing time spent on each node.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == int(n) - 1 and all(len(x.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(u) <= int(n) and 1 <= int(v) <= int(n) and int(u) != int(v) for x in edges)
preconditions.description: edges is a list of n-1 undirected edges (ui, vi) representing connections between nodes (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi).

preconditions.expression: all(int(u) != int(v) for u, v in [(x.split()[0], x.split()[1]) for x in edges])
preconditions.description: No duplicate edges exist in the input.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == max(min(a_dfs[:k]) for a_dfs in dfs_traversals)
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum possible minimum value of the first k nodes in any DFS traversal, where the traversal is determined by choosing any root and any neighbor ordering.

postconditions.expression: a_dfs is a list of node times in DFS order for some root and neighbor ordering
postconditions.description: The DFS traversal is valid for some root and neighbor ordering.
